title: Segmentation hint layer with length-prefixed JSONL for function-call aligned SSE streams
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Context: Several product teams have run into fragile client reassembly when streaming structured outputs (JSON objects, function-call envelopes) over SSE. Small network glitches or proxy trimming of events can split logical JSON objects across SSE chunks. Existing resume mechanisms (Last-Event-ID / resume-token) allow restarting but do not give fine-grained hints about where safe reassembly boundaries exist or how to recover partial structured outputs.

Goal: Define and implement a lightweight "segmentation hint" layer plus a length-prefixed JSONL framing convention for SSE payloads that: 1) preserves backward compatibility for existing SSE clients, 2) enables deterministic reassembly of structured objects and function-call boundaries, 3) provides an optional client-side ack pathway for aggressive low-latency use-cases, and 4) integrates with our reconnect/resume token flow for minimal data re-send and clear observability.

Proposal summary:
- Server-side framing: emit application/jsonl+rw header for streams that will use the new framing. Each logical record (token chunk, partial JSON object, or function-call marker) is wrapped as a length-prefixed JSONL line: "<decimal-length>|<json-object>\n". Example: "124|{\"type\":\"chunk\",\"seq\":42,\"data\":\"...\"}\n". The leading length is the byte length of the JSON payload, not including the prefix or newline. This makes the stream reassembly deterministic in presence of SSE chunk boundaries or mid-message truncation.
- Function-call alignment: the runtime will emit explicit boundary markers as JSON objects with a small set of reserved keys: {"__fc_boundary":true, "call_id":"<uuid>", "phase":"start|end"}. Clients can rely on these markers to reconstruct the exact function-call arguments and result blocks without needing heuristic merging of token streams.
- Segmentation hint header: during the initial response handshake we include an HTTP header: "X-RW-Segmentation: v1;window=256;frag_hint=64;resume=<base64-token>". "window" is the server's preferred number of logical records to keep in the in-memory resume window; "frag_hint" is the recommended maximum bytes for individual fragments the server will produce for optimal client performance. The resume token is an opaque, integrity-protected blob that encodes the last-completed logical-record seq and a compact checksum.
- Reconnect behavior: clients reconnect with the resume token via ?resume=<token> or Last-Event-ID. Server will replay from the last-completed logical-record + 1. If the client holds partial record bytes (length-prefixed) it can supply the partial suffix in a POST to /v1/stream-ack with fields: {resume_token, partial_seq, partial_bytes_base64}. This side-channel is optional and designed for low-latency mobile use-cases where retransmit size matters. Reasons for a side-channel: SSE itself is uni-directional; changing SSE wire to accept client messages is not feasible. The ack endpoint is idempotent and rate-limited.
- Backward compatibility: if client does not opt into JSONL framing header, server will fall back to existing line-based SSE style (legacy). JSONL framing is opt-in by the server per-route and by the client through Accept header. Older clients will continue to work unchanged.

Implementation plan:
1) Runtime serializer change: add a new serializer that emits length-prefixed JSONL records and FC markers. Ensure kernel-level batching does not coalesce multiple records into one monolithic event without preserving prefixes.
2) HTTP header: add X-RW-Segmentation support in the routing layer; token generation and resume semantics implemented in session manager.
3) Acks endpoint: lightweight POST /v1/stream-ack for optional partial reassembly assistance. Implement in control-plane with strict quotas and an ACL for dedicated/private deployments.
4) SDK helpers: update JS/Python SDKs to provide reassembly utilities: read length prefix, buffer until bytes available, parse JSON, surface function-call boundaries, optionally POST partials.
5) Telemetry & metrics: emit events: rw.seg.reassembly_failure, rw.seg.fragment_acked, rw.seg.resume_success, rw.seg.resume_mismatch. Add dashboard and alerts for >0.2% reassembly_failure on canary.

Why length-prefixed JSONL: using a byte-length prefix avoids ambiguity from streamed text encoding or embedded newlines in JSON strings. It keeps the server payload small and makes client parsers deterministic and forgiving to SSE-level truncation or concatenation. This framing also maps cleanly to binary-friendly transports for future websocket fallback.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Complexity: introduces a new framing mode and a server-managed resume token; increases control plane surface area.
- Side-channel acks: useful for mobile clients, but increases server endpoints and potential abuse. Use strict rate-limits and per-session quotas.
- Interop testing: we must verify with common proxies (CloudFlare, AWS ALB, Envoy) that they do not mangle the length prefix. If proxies chunk arbitrarily, prefix still helps but we need header-based hints to avoid timeouts.

Security: resume token must be signed and time-limited to prevent replay across different sessions. Do not encode PII in resume tokens.
acceptance_criteria: Server can serve a route with Content-Type: application/jsonl+rw and produce length-prefixed records
JS and Python SDKs can reassemble partial SSE chunks into full JSON objects and surface function-call markers to the caller API
Reconnect with resume token replays from last-complete-record and does not duplicate completed function-call outputs
Side-channel /v1/stream-ack accepts partial bytes and server resumes without re-sending already-complete records
Metrics for reassembly_failure and resume_success exist and are populated in console (canary monitor)
notes: 2026-03-02 meeting: agreed opt-in framing via Accept header to protect backward compatibility (Ravi, Claire, Samir)
Decision: use decimal length prefix (ASCII) because existing proxies are less likely to mangle ASCII prefixes vs binary headers
Prototype nightlies: serializer implemented behind feature-flag on runtime-unstable; raw throughput unchanged in bench runs for 512-token sequences
Test plan: simulate partial truncation at 1% of packets, validate reassembly success > 99.9% on canary
Developer tasks: runtime serializer, control-plane resume token generator, ack endpoint, JS/Python SDK reassembler, canary dashboard
rollout_plan: Enable on internal staging services and run 72h simulated-network fuzz suite
Canary 2% hosted traffic for non-sensitive routes (console-chat, examples) with alert on rw.seg.reassembly_failure > 0.2%
If stable, ramp to 25% after 48h, 100% after 7 days
Document SDK usage and add migration guide for existing clients
